ideas.title: Same spoon. Twice the salt.
ideas.targetAudience: Home cooks following a recipe that names kosher salt by volume, especially when changing brands.
ideas.whyWatch: Two dimensional spoons and a counterintuitive hook make an everyday seasoning mistake visible.
ideas.visibleEvent: Swipe from an original studio illustration to the exact two-brand tablespoon chart comparison, then a practical substitution check.
ideas.payoff: Learn why Diamond Crystal and Morton’s kosher salt cannot be casually exchanged spoon for spoon; use the recipe’s salt specification or stated grams.

ideas.title: Allspice: one spice or a blend?
ideas.targetAudience: Curious home cooks who encounter allspice in spice cakes, sauces or pickles.
ideas.whyWatch: The familiar pantry name invites a plausible wrong answer; real fruit photography gives a visual clue.
ideas.visibleEvent: Pick one spice or a blend, then swipe to a close fruit study and the reveal: one spice, one tree.
ideas.payoff: Allspice is the dried unripe fruit of Pimenta dioica; its flavor can recall several spices while the ingredient itself is not a blend.

variants.title: Same spoon. Twice the salt.
variants.caption:
Same spoonful, different amount of salt. King Arthur Baking’s chart lists 1 tablespoon of Diamond Crystal kosher salt as 8 g, and Morton’s kosher salt as 16 g. These are published reference values, not a universal measured spoon conversion. Match the recipe’s salt specification, or use its stated gram weight. Original 3D illustration; no live weighing.
Source: https://www.kingarthurbaking.com/learn/ingredient-weight-chart

variants.title: Allspice: one spice or a blend?
variants.caption:
One spice. One tree. Allspice is the dried, unripe fruit of Pimenta dioica—not a spice blend. It can recall cinnamon, clove and nutmeg, and appears in baking, sauces and pickles.
Sources: https://www.spices.res.in/crops/allspice | https://www.nparks.gov.sg/florafaunaweb/flora/6/0/6085
